findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name and verify (against Copilot CLI `--help`/docs) the exact subcommand/flags used to dispatch a non-interactive Arm-B subagent — headless invocation, a single frozen-prompt input, JSON/structured output control, and tool-scoping to grep/read/test-run without rebar tooling — recording each as MATCH/MISMATCH/UNVERIFIED, and route to a SPIKE that dispatches one throwaway Copilot CLI run before committing the full plan.
evidence: Plan: 'a FRESH local harness subagent (Copilot CLI task agent; free, non-Bedrock) receives ONLY: the ticket's AC list verbatim, the worktree path ... and the instruction to verify each AC and emit JSON {ac, verdict...}'

Repo uses Copilot CLI only as a skill-hosting harness: scripts/check_skill_frontmatter.py 'GitHub Copilot CLI ... drops a non-conforming skill'; tests/unit/test_check_skill_frontmatter.py; Makefile:197 — no programmatic headless-dispatch invocation exists in-repo

ABSENCE: no named subcommand/flag (e.g. a `-p`/print/exec/non-interactive mode), no output-format control for JSON, no mechanism cited for constraining tooling to grep/read/test-run while excluding rebar tooling
Evidence class: Unverified — the specific Copilot CLI surface could not be probed and is not exercised anywhere in the repo
findings.finding: Arm B depends on driving the 'Copilot CLI task agent' as a headless, single-prompt-in / structured-JSON-out subagent — a NEW external-CLI integration the repo has not used this way (it currently references Copilot CLI only as a skill-hosting harness in check_skill_frontmatter.py). No subcommand, flag, non-interactive/print mode, or output-format control is named or verified against --help/docs, so the specific CLI surface is UNVERIFIED.
findings.location: Arms → Arm B (treatment): minimal harness agent
scenarios: The named Copilot CLI headless/JSON-emitting mode does not exist or differs from what is assumed, and Arm B cannot be dispatched as specified after the prompt is frozen and Arm A spend has been paid
Copilot CLI has no way to force structured JSON output, so every Arm B run degrades into the harness_error/malformed path — inflating Arm B rejections and confounding the GO/NO-GO rule

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a prior-art paragraph reconciling Arm B with the verifier's harness-native origin recorded in lowchen: state what is materially different this time and how a GO's 'external-harness verifier seam' can be pursued WITHOUT violating lowchen's 'verifier MUST stay harness-independent' constraint (or reframe the GO consequence accordingly).
evidence: Arm B: 'a FRESH local harness subagent (Copilot CLI task agent...) ... plain grep/read/test-run freedom' — this repackages the verifier's original harness-native subagent design.

lowchen north-star: 'The completion verifier began as a SIMPLE harness-native subagent/background agent ... It was reliable. Runaway tool calls and context-window overruns ... only appeared after the transition from harness-native (DSO) to harness-independent (rebar).'
lowchen constraint: 'the verifier MUST stay harness-independent, on the same machinery as the rest of rebar.'

Decision rule GO clause: 'pursue an external-harness verifier seam in production design, feeding viral-peppy-lowchen' — a GO points production toward the exact harness-dependent shape lowchen's constraint forbids, with no reconciliation in the plan.
ABSENCE: the plan cites guanaco and 12b7 as prior art but never cites the DSO→rebar harness-native history that its own treatment arm re-tests.
findings.finding: The plan does not engage the single most directly-relevant prior art: the completion verifier's own harness-native origin, which lowchen records was already tried, was reliable, and was deliberately moved away from — and whose GO conclusion would collide with lowchen's stated harness-independence constraint.
findings.location: Experiment hypothesis / Arms (Arm B) / Predeclared decision rule; cross-ref viral-peppy-lowchen (b4be) description
scenarios: Arm B returns GO, and the operator/lowchen design step must decide whether an external-harness verifier can be adopted at all given the harness-independence constraint — a question the experiment never framed.
A reviewer of the eventual lowchen design asks 'didn't we already have this and move off it, and why?' with no answer recorded in the experiment that motivated the pivot.
findings.suggested_fix: In the hypothesis section, cite lowchen's DSO→rebar history explicitly and note that Arm B is measuring the harness-native design that was previously abandoned; then either (a) narrow the GO consequence to 'import the harness's evidence-assembly/stopping behavior into the harness-INDEPENDENT verifier' rather than adopting an external harness wholesale, or (b) record that the operator has relaxed the harness-independence constraint for this line of work, with a link to that decision.

evidence: 1 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
vague/subjective terms present: sufficient
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Before the first Arm B run, resolve and record the concrete Copilot CLI invocation form (headless/non-interactive dispatch, structured-JSON output guarantee, and actual cost/credit status), and separate a tooling-integration failure from a verification-quality strike so harness_error only counts against Arm B when the tool provably supports the required invocation.
evidence: Arm B: 'a FRESH local harness subagent (Copilot CLI task agent; free, non-Bedrock) receives ONLY ... the instruction to verify each AC and emit JSON {ac, verdict: ..., citations[], reason}'.

Fallback rule: 'On parse failure or missing ACs, retry ... If still malformed/incomplete: record every missing AC as INSUFFICIENT flagged harness_error (counted as rejections for the decision rule — harness fragility is a legitimate strike against Arm B)'.

Retrieved web sources (GitHub Docs 'Copilot CLI command reference'; VS Code / antaoalmada.dev on Copilot custom subagents) confirm Copilot CLI has a subagents mechanism but do NOT confirm headless, non-interactive, single-shot programmatic dispatch that returns deterministic structured JSON — this capability is asserted, not resolved.

ABSENCE: the plan names no CLI invocation form, flag, or output-format guarantee for the Copilot task agent, and does not distinguish a tooling-integration failure from a verification-quality failure.
findings.finding: The plan makes an unverified capability assertion that the GitHub Copilot CLI 'task agent' can be driven headless with a fixed frozen prompt and reliably emit structured one-entry-per-AC JSON; it treats malformed output as an Arm-B quality strike without first confirming the tool supports the invocation mode the experiment depends on.
findings.location: Arms (Arm B) and 'Arm B output validation & fallback'
scenarios: Copilot CLI can only run interactively or cannot be constrained to emit strict JSON, so nearly every rep degrades to harness_error and inflates Arm B's rejection total — driving a NO-GO that reflects integration friction, not verification quality.
The 'free, non-Bedrock' assumption is wrong (Copilot consumes AI credits per the retrieved IDE docs), quietly breaking the 'Arm B uncapped in dollars' premise and the cost comparison.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an Arm-B preflight step that pins the exact Copilot CLI command + output-format contract and does a one-ticket smoke test; if the tool cannot emit strict per-AC JSON headlessly, either wrap it in a thin structured adapter or name a substitute harness, and re-classify pure integration failures out of the decision-rule rejection total.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how a FAILED Arm B rep affects the decision-rule aggregation (e.g. a FAILED-only ticket-variant forces INDETERMINATE, or its ACs count as harness_error rejections) so clauses (i)/(ii) remain computable.
evidence: 'if it crashes again the rep is recorded FAILED (excluded from wall-time medians, included in the report)'
'degrade to 1 rep on the epic if spend requires'
decision rule aggregates 'over the corpus' for false-PASS and rejections
findings.finding: A twice-crashed Arm B subagent is recorded FAILED and 'excluded from wall-time medians, included in the report,' but the plan does not say how a FAILED rep feeds the false-PASS / rejection aggregation the decision rule depends on — if the epic degrades to 1 rep and that rep FAILs, the ticket contributes no Arm B verdicts, leaving clauses (i)/(ii) under-determined.
findings.location: Arm B output validation & fallback + Predeclared decision rule (i)/(ii)
scenarios: Epic run degraded to 1 rep; the sole Arm B rep crashes twice → FAILED → no false-PASS/rejection data for that ticket-variant
Operator must decide whether a missing ticket makes the corpus-aggregate GO evaluable
findings.suggested_fix: Add: 'A ticket-variant whose only surviving Arm B rep is FAILED yields no verdicts; per the fail-closed rule its ACs count as harness_error rejections toward Arm B's rejection total, and false-PASS is scored 0 for those ACs (no coerced PASS possible).'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the Copilot CLI auth precondition (GitHub sign-in / Copilot entitlement) and confirm it is satisfied in the .expscratch run environment before dispatching Arm B.
evidence: Plan asserts 'free, non-Bedrock' and 'local harness free per operator' but states no auth precondition
ABSENCE: no mention of Copilot CLI authentication (GitHub sign-in / Copilot subscription) as a runnability precondition for Arm B
findings.finding: Auth/precondition for the Copilot CLI integration is unstated. The plan calls Arm B 'free, non-Bedrock' (a dollar claim) but does not state that Copilot CLI requires a GitHub login / active Copilot entitlement, nor confirm that entitlement is available in the .expscratch run environment.
findings.location: Arms → Arm B; Budget & reps ('Arm B is uncapped in dollars (local harness free)')
scenarios: The .expscratch environment lacks a signed-in Copilot session, so every Arm B dispatch fails or hangs and is recorded as a failed rep

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the decision rule robust to the known Arm-A agentic variance (35↔55 steps, occasional false-FAILs): e.g. require ≥2 Arm A reps per variant before the epic degrades, aggregate rejection counts as per-rep medians/mins rather than raw sums, or state a minimum-margin threshold on rule (ii) so a single variance-driven false-FAIL cannot flip GO/NO-GO.
evidence: Rule (ii): 'Arm B total rejections on real ACs ... strictly < Arm A total rejections on real ACs'
Plan's own note: 'guanaco observed 2 agentic false-FAILs in one epic run and 35↔55 step variance'
Budget: '2 reps/ticket-variant ... degrade to 1 rep on the epic if spend requires'
A single Arm A false-FAIL (which the plan says occurred in one prior epic run) flips the aggregate inequality when only 1-2 reps are sampled.
findings.finding: The GO decision hinges on a strict-inequality comparison of aggregate rejection totals (rule ii), but the plan's own corpus data establishes Arm A's real-AC rejection count is noise-dominated at the budgeted rep counts, so the decision may be decided by single-run agentic variance rather than a real effect.
findings.location: Predeclared decision rule (ii); Corpus 'Known Arm-A noise'; Budget & reps
scenarios: Arm A epic rep run at 1 rep records the 2 known agentic false-FAILs -> Arm A rejection total inflated -> spurious GO
Arm A epic rep run happens to be clean -> Arm B must beat a near-zero baseline -> spurious NO-GO
